title: India Coaching Staff to Split After Third ODI as Gambhir Weighs Final Call
excerpt: Batting coach Sitanshu Kotak says Gambhir and Sairaj Bahutule are likely to finish the ODI series in Mount Maunganui while he and Morne Morkel open the Test camp in Wellington, but the head coach has the final say.
body:
• According to batting coach Sitanshu Kotak, India's coaching staff is expected to split after the third ODI in Hamilton, with one group finishing the ODI series and the other opening the Test camp.
  • Head coach Gautam Gambhir and spin-bowling coach Sairaj Bahutule are likely to stay with the ODI squad in Mount Maunganui, while Kotak and Morne Morkel head to Wellington.
  • Kotak stressed the plan is not final: Gambhir will make the final decision, and the arrangement can still change.
  • The Wellington camp starts November 11 ahead of the first Test on November 19, while the ODI series closes on November 13 and 15.

India's coaching staff is set to divide into two groups after the third ODI against New Zealand, according to batting coach Sitanshu Kotak, as the tour begins to straddle the end of the one-day series and the start of the two-Test series. Kotak outlined the likely arrangement at a press conference in Hamilton on Monday, while making clear that the details have not been finalised and that head coach Gautam Gambhir will make the final decision.

Under the plan Kotak described, Gambhir and spin-bowling coach Sairaj Bahutule will travel to Mount Maunganui with the ODI squad for the last two matches of the series. Kotak himself and fast-bowling coach Morne Morkel will go the other way, joining the Test squad for a pre-series camp in Wellington, where the first Test begins on November 19. Other support staff will be divided between the two groups.

"[The plan] can still change, but as far as I know, obviously Gautam will have to be here - the one-day World Cup is coming [in 2027], so he will be staying here and probably Sairaj will stay here," Kotak said, as reported by ESPNcricinfo. "Me, Morne and some other staff will go to Wellington. That's the plan, but like I said, Gautam will make the final decision. It can change, but this is how it will likely be."

That is the key decision Gambhir faces: whether to confirm a split that leaves him with the one-day side or to adjust it. The reasoning Kotak gave for Gambhir staying with the ODI group is the 2027 ODI World Cup, which is now a year away and shapes India's white-ball planning even in the middle of a Test build-up. Staying in Mount Maunganui keeps the head coach with the format India are building towards next year, while sending his batting and fast-bowling coaches ahead gives the Test squad senior supervision from the first day of camp.

The Wellington group will not be coaches alone. Kotak and Morkel are expected to leave on November 11 with captain Shubman Gill, KL Rahul, Mohammed Siraj, Anshul Kamboj and Kuldeep Yadav, all members of the Test squad who will not play the fourth and fifth ODIs. The camp is planned for five to six practice sessions, focused, in Kotak's words, on managing loading, fitness and practice and doing as much preparation as the conditions permit. Gambhir and Bahutule would then travel to Wellington on November 16, the day after the fifth ODI, to rejoin the full group before the first Test.

Kotak said his own work in Wellington will centre on phase-based preparation for the batters, planning for batting first or second and for third- and fourth-innings situations, and tailoring conversations to individual batters, from Yashasvi Jaiswal to KL Rahul, Gill and Rishabh Pant. He noted that the ODI pitches had already offered useful clues, with swing early, seam movement after four to six overs and some awkward bounce.

What happens next will confirm whether the reported split holds. The third ODI is in Hamilton on Tuesday, November 10. The ODI series then finishes in Mount Maunganui on November 13 and 15, while the Test camp runs in Wellington from November 11. The first Test starts at the Basin Reserve on November 19, followed by the second Test in Christchurch from November 27.
